newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economy picking up, on course for EMU - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: German economy picking up, on course for EMU - Kohl.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that Germany's domestic economy was picking up speed and would grow by 2-1/2 percent this year and by as much as three percent in 1998.

Kohl, according to the text of remarks released before a news conference, also said Germany would fulfil the convergence criteria for Europe's single currency and that the euro would be launched, as planned, at the start of 1999.

"We expect real growth of 2-1/2 percent this year. For 1998 there are signs that growth will be up to three percent," Kohl said. "The main motor is exports. I am convinced that the domestic economy is gaining momentum."
Kohl also said he was convinced that Germany would make the grade for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"For me it is clear: Germany will fulfil the criteria. The euro will come at the agreed time," he said.

Separately, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in Munich that Germany would manage to cut its budget deficit this year to three percent of gross domestic product -- the Maastricht treaty limit -- despite pressures on the budget.
